g.text: Front channel goes through the user's browser and is visible. Back channel is server-to-server.
FRONT CHANNEL — via the browser, anyone can see it
4) redirect back with a one-time CODE
6) access token (+ refresh token, + ID token for OIDC)
BACK CHANNEL — server to server, the browser never sees this
Why a code and not a token
Step 4's code travels through the browser, so it can be stolen.
On its own it's useless: step 5 also needs the verifier
(never sent in step 2) and the client secret.
PKCE was built for mobile apps, which can't keep a secret.
It's now recommended for every client type, including web.
